Risk officer assessment, BOXY (ORGANIC class, age 31 min, alive):

Pool depth is 145 SOL and last-15-min volume is about $143k, so a $20 ticket is about 0.01% of recent volume and well under 1% of pool value. Slippage is not the constraint; base rates are.

Red flags: bundle share 48.7% and a launch bot present in the first two minutes, plus a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.79 right after graduation. Those are not clean organic signals. Net flow over 15 min is only +31 SOL against 586 SOL sold, so the 30% move is being carried by heavy two-way churn.

Recommendation: refuse. The bundling and bot activity fall outside the organic profile the desk is looking for, and the 23% pullback from the 30-minute high suggests distribution, not a base. If the desk insists on buying anyway, use the minimum $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying BOXY now is thin, and the brief itself shows why.

What points toward real demand: the coin is alive at 31 minutes, the last 15 minutes show 572 buyers and $143k volume, net flow is positive (+31 SOL), the 30-minute return is +140%, and the top-3 holders hold only 16.6%, with no airdrop dump seen. The pool depth of 145 SOL is workable for a $20 ticket.

What undercuts it: 49% of the curve came from bundled buys, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.79, meaning sellers were active early. The 23% drawdown from the 30-minute high and the 499 sellers in the last 15 minutes suggest the post-graduation rally is already being distributed. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% also eat into any short-term bounce.

Verdict: no strong case. Bundled supply and heavy selling into a fading high match the pattern that has lost money for most buyers in this window. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is distribution by early holders into the recent bounce. The 30-minute return is +140%, but the last 15 minutes show 586 SOL sold against 618 bought, with net flow of only +31 SOL and 499 sellers versus 572 buyers. That is heavy two-way churn, not a fresh wave of conviction. The curve data points the same way: bundle share is 48.7% and the completer share is 11.9%, so a large slice of supply was accumulated early by linked wallets that have every reason to sell into strength. The 23% drawdown from the 30-minute high already shows the top is not holding. Pool depth of 145 SOL means a $20 round trip faces the upper end of the 1.4-5.1% cost band, and a 6-10% bounce gets consumed by fees and impact before it pays. Skip.
